import json
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from datetime import datetime
import numpy as np

with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

def parse_series(series_data):
    dates = [datetime.strptime(d['date'], '%Y-%m') for d in series_data['data']]
    values = [d['value'] for d in series_data['data']]
    return dates, values

dates_cpi, vals_cpi = parse_series(data['cpi_inflation'])
dates_wage, vals_wage = parse_series(data['wage_growth'])
dates_ffr, vals_ffr = parse_series(data['federal_funds_rate'])
dates_rwg, vals_rwg = parse_series(data['real_wage_growth'])

# Editorial color palette
color_cpi = '#D64045'       # warm red
color_wage = '#1B6B93'      # teal blue
color_ffr = '#2D3142'       # dark slate (near black)
color_rwg = '#E9A820'       # golden amber
color_neg_fill = '#D64045'  # red fill for negative real wages
color_pos_fill = '#4A9B6E'  # green fill for positive real wages

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.sans-serif': ['DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica'],
    'axes.linewidth': 0.8,
    'xtick.major.width': 0.6,
    'ytick.major.width': 0.6,
    'xtick.minor.width': 0.4,
    'ytick.minor.width': 0.4,
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 7.5), dpi=180)
fig.set_facecolor('#FAFAFA')
ax.set_facecolor('#FAFAFA')

# Fill for real wage squeeze (negative region)
zeros = [0] * len(vals_rwg)
ax.fill_between(dates_rwg, vals_rwg, zeros,
                where=[v < 0 for v in vals_rwg],
                color=color_neg_fill, alpha=0.10, interpolate=True,
                zorder=1, label='_nolegend_')
ax.fill_between(dates_rwg, vals_rwg, zeros,
                where=[v >= 0 for v in vals_rwg],
                color=color_pos_fill, alpha=0.08, interpolate=True,
                zorder=1, label='_nolegend_')

# Peak inflation zone highlight (May–Jul 2022)
peak_start = datetime(2022, 4, 1)
peak_end = datetime(2022, 8, 1)
ax.axvspan(peak_start, peak_end, color='#D64045', alpha=0.07, zorder=0)

# Rate hike lag annotation zone
hike_start = datetime(2022, 3, 1)
inflation_decline_start = datetime(2022, 7, 1)
lag_y = 10.0
ax.annotate('', xy=(inflation_decline_start, lag_y), xytext=(hike_start, lag_y),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='#555555', lw=1.2, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))
ax.text(datetime(2022, 5, 1), lag_y + 0.25, 'Policy\nlag',
        ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=7.5, color='#555555',
        fontstyle='italic', linespacing=0.9)

# Main series
ax.plot(dates_cpi, vals_cpi, color=color_cpi, linewidth=2.3, zorder=5, solid_capstyle='round')
ax.plot(dates_wage, vals_wage, color=color_wage, linewidth=2.0, zorder=4, solid_capstyle='round')
ax.plot(dates_ffr, vals_ffr, color=color_ffr, linewidth=2.3, zorder=6,
        linestyle='-', solid_capstyle='round', drawstyle='steps-post')
ax.plot(dates_rwg, vals_rwg, color=color_rwg, linewidth=1.8, zorder=4,
        linestyle='--', dash_capstyle='round')

# Zero line for real wage growth reference
ax.axhline(y=0, color='#888888', linewidth=0.6, linestyle=':', zorder=2)

# Peak CPI annotation
peak_idx = vals_cpi.index(max(vals_cpi))
ax.annotate(f'CPI peak: {vals_cpi[peak_idx]:.1f}%',
            xy=(dates_cpi[peak_idx], vals_cpi[peak_idx]),
            xytext=(dates_cpi[peak_idx] + (dates_cpi[1]-dates_cpi[0])*3, vals_cpi[peak_idx] + 0.8),
            fontsize=8, color=color_cpi, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color_cpi, lw=1.0, shrinkB=3),
            zorder=10)

# Real wage trough annotation
trough_idx = vals_rwg.index(min(vals_rwg))
ax.annotate(f'Real wage trough: {vals_rwg[trough_idx]:.1f}%',
            xy=(dates_rwg[trough_idx], vals_rwg[trough_idx]),
            xytext=(dates_rwg[trough_idx] + (dates_rwg[1]-dates_rwg[0])*4, vals_rwg[trough_idx] - 1.2),
            fontsize=8, color='#B8860B', fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#B8860B', lw=1.0, shrinkB=3),
            zorder=10)

# Mark where real wages recover to positive
for i in range(1, len(vals_rwg)):
    if vals_rwg[i-1] < 0 and vals_rwg[i] >= 0:
        recovery_date = dates_rwg[i]
        ax.plot(recovery_date, vals_rwg[i], 'o', color=color_pos_fill,
                markersize=7, zorder=8, markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1.2)
        ax.annotate(f'Recovery\n{recovery_date.strftime("%b %Y")}',
                    xy=(recovery_date, vals_rwg[i]),
                    xytext=(recovery_date + (dates_rwg[1]-dates_rwg[0])*2.5, vals_rwg[i] + 1.5),
                    fontsize=7.5, color=color_pos_fill, fontweight='bold',
                    ha='center',
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color_pos_fill, lw=0.9, shrinkB=3),
                    zorder=10)
        break

# FFR peak annotation
ffr_peak_val = max(vals_ffr)
ffr_peak_idx = vals_ffr.index(ffr_peak_val)
ax.annotate(f'FFR plateau: {ffr_peak_val:.2f}%',
            xy=(dates_ffr[ffr_peak_idx], ffr_peak_val),
            xytext=(dates_ffr[ffr_peak_idx] + (dates_ffr[1]-dates_ffr[0])*3, ffr_peak_val + 1.0),
            fontsize=8, color=color_ffr, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color_ffr, lw=1.0, shrinkB=3),
            zorder=10)

# First rate hike marker
for i in range(1, len(vals_ffr)):
    if vals_ffr[i] > vals_ffr[i-1] + 0.1:
        ax.plot(dates_ffr[i], vals_ffr[i], 's', color=color_ffr,
                markersize=6, zorder=8, markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=1.0)
